1.explanation:
1. components/prism-shell-session.js & .min.js: These two files define the shell-session grammar. The broken behavior—only a single output token—points directly to a failure in this grammar (e.g. missing dependency on Bash, altered regexes, or a faulty extend() call). 
2. components/index.js: This file declares language metadata and dependencies for every component. If shell-session’s “require” field was changed or omitted here, the Bash grammar won’t be loaded first, breaking the shell-session tokenizer.  
3. components.js: This autogenerated registry is used by the download builder to assemble the right language scripts. If index.js metadata for shell-session is wrong, components.js will carry that mistake into the bundled download, so the tokenizer never gets the patterns it needs.
1.bug_scenario: The user’s screenshots show that when highlighting a shell session block (class language-shell-session) with Prism 1.22 or 1.23 from the download page, the entire block is wrapped in a single token.output span. Historically (and in an earlier 1.22 build), Prism would correctly tokenize the prompt, commands (echo, exit), strings (\"Hello World\"), and output separately. The DOM tree reveals only the fallback “output” pattern matching everything. This indicates that the shell-session grammar isn’t being loaded or its patterns no longer match, so only the generic output rule applies.

2.explanation: The grammar for the “shell-session” language lives in prism-shell-session.js (and its minified counterpart). These files define the regular expressions and token hierarchy that split prompts, commands, arguments, and output into separate tokens. If they are broken or omitted during download generation, the shell-session tokenizer will never match input lines and will fall back to treating everything as output. Fixing or restoring the correct regex patterns in these files will re-enable proper tokenization.
2.bug_scenario: When using Prism’s web-downloaded builds (v1.22 and v1.23) or the Test Drive page with the “language-shell-session” class, input lines (the shell prompt and commands) are no longer tokenized separately from output. Instead, everything is lumped into a single “output” token, so none of the prompts or commands are highlighted. In earlier downloads of v1.22 this worked correctly. The DOM inspection shows only one <span class="token output"> wrapping the entire session block, indicating that the shell-session grammar never ran its input/command patterns.
